title: Keep credentials out of public code and responses
statement: No API key, token, connection string, private endpoint, or internal identifier appears in a client bundle, an inline script, a metadata value, a comment, or a committed configuration file that ships to the browser.
rationale: Anything delivered to the browser is public regardless of how obscure its location is, and a credential published this way stays compromised until it is rotated, not until the code is changed.
implementation: Keep server-only values out of the variable prefix the framework exposes to the client, read them only in server code paths, and scan the built output for credential-shaped strings before release. A value already shipped must be rotated, not merely removed.

verification.method: Search the built client bundles and the served responses for credential patterns and for the names of server-only configuration variables.

caution: The cited reference is a community security guideline rather than a specification, so this record is tier B. What it asserts - that anything delivered to the browser is public - is a property of the delivery mechanism and is not in dispute.

title: Detect injected links and unauthorized redirects
statement: The site can tell whether the links, redirects, and markup it serves are the ones its own code produced, and it inspects the served output rather than only the repository.
rationale: Injected content is placed where the site's authors will not look - inside a template fragment, behind a user-agent condition, in a database field rendered as markup - so its presence is only visible in what is actually served.
implementation: Crawl the production site on a schedule, extract the outbound link hosts and redirect targets, and compare them against an allowed set the site declares. Investigate any new external host rather than adding it to the set.

verification.method: Compare the outbound hosts and redirect targets found by crawling production against the declared allowed set, including requests made with a crawler user agent.

title: Declare a transport security policy on the production origin
statement: The production origin sends a Strict-Transport-Security header with a deliberate maximum age, and the decision about whether subdomains are included is recorded rather than inherited from an example.
rationale: Without the header the first request of a visit can still be attempted over the insecure scheme, and the redirect that fixes it happens after that request has already been sent.
implementation: Set the header at the edge or the server that terminates TLS, starting with a short maximum age and lengthening it once nothing breaks. Include subdomains only after confirming every subdomain can serve over the secure scheme, because the directive cannot be withdrawn from clients that already received it.

verification.method: Request the production origin and record the presence, maximum age, and subdomain scope of the header, then confirm each subdomain serves over the secure scheme.

caution: The subdomain directive and preloading are effectively irreversible for the lifetime of the declared maximum age, so this record deliberately does not classify the change as safe to apply automatically.

title: Reject redirect targets the application does not own
statement: Any route that redirects to a destination taken from a request parameter validates that destination against a list of permitted paths or hosts, and refuses rather than redirects when it does not match.
rationale: An unvalidated redirect lets any party publish a link on the site's own origin that lands somewhere else, which lends the site's reputation to whatever the destination turns out to be.
implementation: Compare the requested destination against an allowed list rather than checking for a prefix, since a prefix check is defeated by a host that begins with the expected string. Prefer passing an identifier that maps to a destination server-side over passing the destination itself.

verification.method: Request each redirecting route with an external host, a scheme-relative host, and an encoded variant as the destination, and record the resulting status and location.

caution: The cited reference is a community security guideline rather than a platform document, which is why this record is tier B. The mechanism itself is not in dispute.

title: Keep source maps and debug output off production responses
statement: Production responses do not carry source maps, stack traces, framework debug panels, verbose error bodies, or directory listings.
rationale: Each of these describes the internals of the running application to anyone who asks, and an error body naming a query or a file path turns a routine failure into a description of how to reach the data behind it.
implementation: Disable map emission for the production build or upload the maps to the error reporting service without serving them, and return a generic error body while logging the detail server-side. Confirm the framework is running in its production mode, since debug output usually follows from that setting alone.

verification.method: Request the map path for each built bundle and trigger a handled and an unhandled error, recording the status and body returned in each case.

caution: Some teams publish maps deliberately to aid error reporting. That is a defensible choice, so this record asks for the decision to be explicit rather than treating any exposure as a defect.

title: Prevent user input from reaching indexing directives
statement: No value a reader can supply is interpolated into a canonical link, a robots directive, a language alternate, a sitemap entry, or a structured data document.
rationale: These constructs are the site's own statements about how its pages should be treated, so allowing an outside party to influence them hands over control of the site's indexing to whoever can submit a form.
implementation: Build these values from route definitions and configuration only, never from a query parameter, a submitted field, or a stored value an unprivileged account can edit. Where a stored value must contribute, validate it against a closed set before use.

verification.method: Submit crafted input through every field and parameter that reaches a template, then inspect the canonical link, directives, and structured data in the resulting response.

caution: The cited document defines the directives rather than prohibiting untrusted input in them, so this record is tier B. It follows from the directives being statements by the site operator.
